title: Google freezes open-source bug bounty program amid flood of invalid AI slop submissions — product flaw submissions halted until 2027 as maintainers drown in hallucinations
key_facts: Google suspended product vulnerability submissions to its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program (OSS VRP), announced in an X post on 1 Oct 2026, effective the same day.

Reason given: an influx of invalid AI-generated reports; Google engineers and open-source maintainers were reportedly swamped by thousands of reports describing bugs that did not exist or could not be exploited.
Google says it will give an update by the first quarter of 2027 while it reworks this part of the program and pointed researchers to its other reward programs.
Reports submitted before 1 Oct are not affected; supply chain reports to OSS VRP continue; some Google Cloud repositories may still be covered through the Cloud VRP.

Tom's Hardware places it in a wider pattern: Linux kernel maintainers said they were overwhelmed by AI-found CVEs (about 2,000 per release) and Intel suspended its own bug bounty, without officially naming AI reports as the cause.
quote_evidence: Google has officially suspended product vulnerability submissions to its Open Source Software Vulnerability Reward Program (OSS VRP) — a bug bounty program — over an influx of invalid AI-driven reports.
The suspension went into effect on October 1 — the day of the announcement — and does not affect product vulnerabilities submitted before that date.
Google said it may still accept reports covering product vulnerabilities through the Cloud VRP, “for some Google Cloud repos impacting Google Cloud products.”
why_it_matters_hint: A major bug bounty closing a door because AI-written false reports cost more maintainer time than they save shows the open-source security pipeline is being clogged, not helped, by automated bug hunting.
notes: Announcement was 1 Oct 2026, article 3 Oct: two days before the window, so scored down one and marked follow-up. The 'maintainers overwhelmed' detail is reported ('reportedly'), the suspension itself is official. Linux and Intel comparisons are the outlet's context, Intel's reason unconfirmed.
